newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo drops on profit-taking after results.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo drops on profit-taking after results.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc were 2.3 percent lower by midmorning on Thursday amid profit-taking after a slightly disappointing results statement, dealers said.

The shares were down 24-1/2p at 10.10-1/2 stg by 1049 GMT, even as the FTSE index -- in which it is one of the biggest constituents -- was up 26.0 points at 4,386.1, after earlier setting a record 4,393.2.
With the 18 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 2.96 billion stg no better than analysts expected, some said there were signs of slight disappointment over the growth rates of new products.
"If you look at the statement you will see that the new products are perhaps not doing so well as hoped and I have a feeling people will pick up on that," said one senior dealer.
"The stock has had a good run but if people want to be in the sector maybe they will want to be switching out of Glaxo and into something else," the dealer said.

However others said Thursday's decline in the shares was no more than profit-taking after recent strong gains -- the stock had jumped 32 percent from its mid-January low by Wednesday's intraday record of 10.63 stg.

Glaxo chief Richard Sykes warned that sales growth would be in a "low single digit" range for 1997 and 1998 but another dealer said that was just a precautionary message which did not necessarily directly bear on profits.

"He's just saying that it will be difficult to make a major advance while major products are in decline," the dealer said, "sales growth of new drugs does tend to be a bit patchy and Zantac sales are declining, but we have known that for years."

"The stock has run up very strongly, I just think one should be careful before making too great an interpretation on the pre-tax level and Glaxo does have a good yield compared with others in the sector."
By 1120 GMT the stock had rebounded to be down just 9p at 10.26 stg. Trading volume was heavy at 11.8 million shares.
